note: Transcribed from tree-sitter-markdown's scanner.c read as a specification.
Nothing is linked. Line references are to the pinned copy under
The C packs three flags into one uint8_t `state` and this splits them into
three registers, because the algebra has no bit tests and does not want
any: a packed byte was the C's way of fitting a serialize buffer, not a
fact about the scanner. Same information, one comparison each.
The sixteen LIST_ITEM_*_INDENTATION enum values are one kind and a width.
The C unfolds them arithmetically itself (`list_item_indentation`, :99),
so this stores the width in the frame where it belongs.

registers.3: matched   - how many open blocks this line has matched (:209)
registers.5: fence     - the open fence's delimiter length (:216)

rules.name: eof_is_a_terminal_where_one_is_admitted
rules.why: :1332 - the C asks this *before* the block-close fallback below, so a state that admits `_eof` gets `_eof` and never the close; zero width, and the frames are left standing for whoever closes them

rules.name: eof_closes_every_open_block
rules.why: :1331 - a file ending inside open blocks owes one close each

rules.name: match_block_quote
rules.why: :382 match(BLOCK_QUOTE) - blanks, a '>', and then one optional blank whose width past the first is kept: `indentation += advance(s, lexer) - 1`, which is 0 for a space and 3 for a tab

rules.name: match_indented_code
rules.why: :336 match(INDENTED_CODE_BLOCK) - four columns, and the line must have something on it

rules.name: match_list_item_indented
rules.why: :366 - the item's own stored indentation, spent out of the budget

rules.name: match_list_item_empty
rules.why: :377 - an item's line that just ends matches at any indentation

rules.name: match_fenced
rules.why: :395 match(FENCED_CODE_BLOCK) - unconditional, consuming nothing

rules.name: match_anonymous
rules.why: :396 - the same arm for ANONYMOUS; one body each rather than a switch

rules.name: close_block_after_blank_line
rules.why: grammar.json `_html_block_6`/`_7` end on a newline then a blank line, and only *then* `_close_block` - so this answers at the start of the line after the blank one, which is what `lull` asks. The scanner itself pushes only ANONYMOUS (:1039 and friends) and never learns which html variety is open - the parse table does, through `valid_symbols` - so the end markers of varieties 1 to 5 (`-->`, `?>`, `>`, `]]>`, ``) are permission-driven and are not transcribed here. The blank line is not: it is a byte fact, and it is what closes the two varieties nothing else can close.

rules.name: block_continuation
rules.why: :1434-1456 - one pass over the open blocks, one answer. The cursor survives in reg 3, so a parser that asks again resumes where this stopped, exactly as `s->matched` does.

rules.name: close_unmatched_block
rules.why: :1459 - nothing matched and the last break was not soft, so close one. :1462 leaves the matching state when the cursor has caught up with the stack, and it asks *after* the pop - so the depth this reads is the popped one, which is why the set comes second.

rules.name: lazy_continuation
rules.why: :1445 - a block failed to match after a soft break, which is a lazy paragraph continuation: leave the matching state and close nothing

rules.name: matching_done
rules.why: :1452 - every open block matched, so leave the matching state. The cursor is *not* cleared here: the C zeroes `s->matched` only at the next line ending, and the rules that ask `matched == open_blocks.size` (setext, the lazy markers) read it in between.

rules.name: blank_line_start
rules.why: :1374 - zero width on purpose, the characters are not consumed

rules.name: line_ending_behind_the_line_s_own_blanks
rules.why: :1345 the not-matching branch advances over the line's leading blanks before it looks at anything, so by the time the `break` at :1380 falls through to :1542 the lookahead is the newline the soak stopped on and the token covers the blanks the C had already eaten. Sits behind `blank_line_start` for the same reason the C's `break` sits behind it, and is gated on `blank` because that is the only shape reaching :1542 from here - which is also the shape `soft_line_ending` declines (:1483 wants `not_blank`), so the two never race

rules.name: indented_chunk_start
rules.why: :1358 - four columns of lead and something on the line

rules.name: block_quote_start
rules.why: :571 - a '>' with at most three columns of lead

rules.name: atx_heading
rules.why: :587 - one to six hashes then a space or the line end; the count picks which of six terminals, exactly the classifier yaml also needs

rules.name: thematic_break_star
rules.why: :463 parse_star - three or more, nothing else on the line

rules.name: thematic_break_dash
rules.why: :798 parse_minus - the same, and it loses to a setext underline

rules.name: thematic_break_underscore
rules.why: :546 parse_thematic_break_underscore - underscores never list-mark

rules.name: setext_h1_underline
rules.why: :608 - only where every open block matched this line

rules.name: fenced_code_block_end_backtick
rules.why: :415 - a close outranks an open where both would fit, and needs at least as many backticks as the open had

rules.name: fenced_code_block_end_tilde
rules.why: :415 - the same over tildes; the two families never close each other

rules.name: html_block_1_start
rules.why: :1036 - a `<pre`/`<script`/`<style` opens a raw-text block

rules.name: html_block_4_start
rules.why: :969 - `<!` and a capital

rules.name: html_block_6_start
rules.why: :1054 - a tag from rule 7's roster of 62 block-level names

rules.name: html_block_7_start
rules.why: :1161 - any complete tag alone on its line. Not a paragraph interrupt (:162), which is the whole difference between it and the six above.

rules.name: fenced_code_block_start_backtick
rules.why: :402 - three or more backticks open a fence and remember how many

rules.name: fenced_code_block_start_tilde
rules.why: :402 with delimiter '~'

rules.name: list_marker_minus_dont_interrupt
rules.why: :831-835 - one marker and nothing but the line end after it, with every open block matched: the empty item that may not interrupt a paragraph.

rules.name: list_marker_minus
rules.why: :798 - a marker, tried after the thematic break it can be confused with

rules.name: list_marker_plus_dont_interrupt
rules.why: :831-835 - one marker and nothing but the line end after it, with every open block matched: the empty item that may not interrupt a paragraph.

rules.name: list_marker_plus
rules.why: :628 parse_plus

rules.name: list_marker_star_dont_interrupt
rules.why: :831-835 - one marker and nothing but the line end after it, with every open block matched: the empty item that may not interrupt a paragraph.

rules.name: list_marker_star
rules.why: :463 parse_star, after the thematic break arm

rules.name: list_marker_dot_dont_interrupt
rules.why: :745-767 - `dont_interrupt` is decided by the bytes and the organs alone: a second digit or a bare marker line, and every open block already matched. It is a different terminal, not a different width, so the parse table can forbid a list here while allowing one where a paragraph is not being interrupted.

rules.name: list_marker_dot
rules.why: :730 parse_ordered_list_marker - at most nine digits, per the spec

rules.name: list_marker_parenthesis_dont_interrupt
rules.why: :745-767 - `dont_interrupt` is decided by the bytes and the organs alone: a second digit or a bare marker line, and every open block already matched. It is a different terminal, not a different width, so the parse table can forbid a list here while allowing one where a paragraph is not being interrupted.

rules.name: list_marker_parenthesis
rules.why: :730 with a ')' terminator

rules.name: setext_h2_underline
rules.why: :608 with '-'; below the list marker because a lone '-' is a marker

rules.name: soft_line_ending
rules.why: :1483 - a break inside a paragraph: the line being ended is not blank (a blank line is not inside a paragraph, so the grammar wants `_blank_line_start` then a hard `_line_ending`) and nothing on the next line would interrupt it. The C asks by calling its own scan with a constant permission set; `fires` is that constant array read as the named set of rules it is. :1520 - the matching state is entered only if the simulated pass says one open block *will* match, so `pass ... after` is that look-ahead and `min 1 pass.ran` is `one_will_be_matched`. :1507 - the interrupt scan runs on **one lexer**, after the matching pass consumed the open blocks' own markers, so it is anchored where that pass stopped and reads the indentation it left: a `>` on the next line of an open block quote is that quote's continuation and the scan never sees it.

rules.name: line_ending
rules.why: :1542 - every other break. :1551 - it re-enters the matching state only when there is an open block to match, which is what `min 1 frames.depth` says.
